title: Digital access: choose FNMT certificate or Cl@ve
intro: Spain uses several accepted electronic-identification methods. The FNMT citizen certificate and Cl@ve are separate systems: the certificate is installed on your device, while Cl@ve identifies you through the government's shared login system. A portal decides which methods it accepts, so regular residents often benefit from setting up both.
status: National digital-access tools · accepted methods depend on each service

items.label: Procedure
items.text: Choose the FNMT Certificado de Persona Física, register in Cl@ve, or set up both. One does not automatically create the other.

items.label: Where to go
items.text: For FNMT, use the official FNMT electronic office: configure the device, submit the certificate request, receive the request code, prove your identity and then download the certificate. For Cl@ve, start from the official Cl@ve registration service. If you need an in-person appointment, direct AEAT and Seguridad Social appointment links are below. For AEAT Cl@ve registration, choose Other procedures → Electronic identification → Register in Cl@ve. For FNMT identity accreditation, first check the FNMT accreditation-office guidance because not every public office or appointment category performs FNMT accreditation.

items.label: Which one to choose
bullets: FNMT certificate: useful when a portal accepts certificate-based identification or electronic signing; some procedures also use AutoFirma.
Cl@ve Móvil: convenient for routine identification on services integrated with Cl@ve, using the app/QR confirmation flow.
Cl@ve Permanente: designed for frequent access with a lasting password; higher-security services can add a one-time SMS code.
For the widest practical fallback, set up both if you are eligible. The specific portal always decides what it accepts.

items.label: Registration and cost
items.text: Neither route uses Modelo 790. The FNMT citizen certificate itself is free. Cl@ve has basic and advanced registration levels; basic registration does not unlock every service or Cl@ve Firma. Optional FNMT mobile video identification is a separate paid identity-verification service and is currently limited to a valid Spanish DNI.

items.label: Prepare
bullets: Your DNI or NIE and the identity document required by the chosen route
For the standard FNMT office route: the request code sent by email
EU citizens using FNMT: NIE evidence plus passport or national identity document, as required by FNMT
A mobile phone number and email address for Cl@ve registration
For FNMT software certificate: keep using the same computer and user account from request through download

items.label: What happens after
items.text: After FNMT identity accreditation, download the certificate using the same computer and user account used for the request, then make a protected backup. After Cl@ve registration, you can use Cl@ve Móvil and, if needed, activate Cl@ve Permanente. Some higher-security functions require advanced registration, and not every public service offers every identification method.
